tree.name: Fair
tree.blurb: From the gold-laced dust of its western canyons to the haunted glaciers of the far north, Fair is a land of adventure and antiquity. Chart a course through newly-opened fjord kingdoms, navigate the politics of ancient empires, and unearth the secrets of a world shaped by heroes and forgotten evils.
tree.selectorDescription: The world of Fair, from western canyons to haunted northern ice.

children.selectorDescription: A frozen northern frontier of auroras, survival towns, glacier ruins, and post-winter scars.
children.summary: A northern arctic tundra of frozen coasts, hard frontier villages, auroras, and old dangers left behind by the Endless Winter.
children.description: Icebeach lies far northwest of Fair, where coastal towns cling to frozen beaches and the habitable world gives way to permafrost, glacier, and polar sea. Nine years after the Endless Winter broke, its people remain split between the Frozen, hardened survivors of the long dark, and the Thawed, newcomers drawn by trade, mining, wine, fish, and other opportunities exposed by the melt.

children.name: Castgate
children.blurb: Encased within a dome that holds the winter at bay, Castgate's picturesque beauty was earned through legendary battles against a goddess and an undead horde. Though its streets bustle with prosperity from gems and ships, the common folk work in the shadow of the very magic that shelters them.
children.selectorDescription: A prosperous dome-city that endures winter under old magic.

children.name: Southern Thalassia
children.blurb: Southern Thalassia is a significant maritime region characterized by a series of islands formed and scared by the 'Night of Falling Stars,' an event wherein lunar and asteroidal fragments impacted the region, depositing exotic minerals and creating unique geological formations. This celestial deposition has resulted in altered atmospheric conditions, residual magical energies, and a notable biodiversity influenced by stellar radiation, making the region a focal point for historical study, resource acquisition (particularly rare minerals and energy concentrations), and contested maritime activity, including piracy, with various factions vying for control over these transformed territories.  This map is still under devlopment.
children.selectorDescription: An unfinished maritime map of star-scarred islands and pirate waters.

children.name: Cursed-Old-Lin
children.blurb: Imprisoned by mist, this land groans under an undying tyrant's shadow. Jagged peaks claw at a twilight sky; the ancient woods conceal secrets best left buried. Above all, Castle Ravenloft looms, a monument to sorrow. Here, despair stains the very soil, and all are ensnared by Strahd.
children.selectorDescription: A mist-choked cursed land where Strahd's shadow still lingers.

children.name: Gelwood
children.blurb: Located on the southern side of the Ardoise Mountains and just off the old Chemin de Ronceval (Ronceval Road), Gelwood is a town defined by resilience. This revived frontier settlement is built upon the moss-covered stone foundations of a much older, forgotten settlement. In the last handful of years, hardy settlers from Rockdrift and Ironstream have begun to reclaim the ruins, building their homes and livelihoods amidst the ghosts of the past. It is now a burgeoning community of farmers, woodcutters, fur traders, and ambitious prospectors, all drawn by persistent tales of gold, platinum, and even diamonds hidden in the nearby mountains.

searchIndex.name: IceBeach
searchIndex.summary: A frozen northern frontier of auroras, survival towns, glacier ruins, and post-winter scars.
searchIndex.description: Icebeach lies far northwest of Fair, where coastal towns cling to frozen beaches and the habitable world gives way to permafrost, glacier, and polar sea. Nine years after the Endless Winter broke, its people remain split between the Frozen, hardened survivors of the long dark, and the Thawed, newcomers drawn by trade, mining, wine, fish, and other opportunities exposed by the melt.

searchIndex.name: Castgate
searchIndex.summary: Icebeach's sheltered trade hub, warmed by the rebuilt Firmament and divided between old survivors and wealthy newcomers.
searchIndex.description: Castgate is a paradox in the north: a humid, flower-scented town beneath a magical dome while salt, ice, wind, mines, and political ambition press against the barrier outside.
searchIndex.searchText: The Firmament The dome was first built by Averios Calytheron, shattered during Morena's assault in the Eternal Winter, and rebuilt after the thaw. Inside, it mimics a clear blue sky and turns Castgate into a tropical-seeming refuge against the polar night. Tension The comfort of the dome has become a social fault line. Locals remember survival, Sub Rosa, and old losses, while the Thawed, southern merchants, Athenaeum agents, and wealthy visitors increasingly treat the town as opportunity. Notable places The Frozen Rose anchors adventuring and Sub Rosa memory; Bleak's Stand memorializes the dead; the Shrine of Hestia, Frostviel, the Crystal Needle, the Groves of Hope's Rebirth, and the docks all give the town more than a single civic center. City IceBeach Firmament Harbor Gemstone mines Athenaeum Sub Rosa Reconstruction Map IceBeach Guide spelling Casgate Shelter The Firmament Industries Shipbuilding, fishing, gemstone mining, trade Leadership Tolin Stillgrove shaped the reconstruction era

searchIndex.name: Flamore
searchIndex.summary: A ruined mountain school whose experiments turned from celestial study toward forbidden glacier secrets.
searchIndex.description: Flamore's School of Experimental Wizardry began as a remote magical redoubt and later became a school, but its turn toward forbidden research under the mountains ended in catastrophe.
searchIndex.searchText: History The Flamore family built the castle as a private redoubt before Gilded Nations backing formalized it as a school. It originally studied the heavens under Nyx, then shifted toward darker research after a strange timeline-crossing event. The incident Exploration beneath the castle uncovered vile tombs, glacier-connected cave systems, and an artifact called the orbit of subnecromancy. Containment failed, zombifying the people inside the wards. Current status The ruins remain a warning against academic arrogance, glacier-delving, and treating cosmic horror as a research opportunity. searchIndex.name: Fractured Point
searchIndex.summary: A walled crag town, lighthouse, trade stop, and first arrival point for many visitors to Icebeach.
searchIndex.description: Fractured Point perches above rocky shores where stained-glass lanterns fight the wind and a castle beacon watches the icefield plains.
searchIndex.searchText: At a glance The town can look festive from a distance, with colored lanterns twisting over narrow streets, but the wind has worn away much of its welcome. Local mood Common folk carry the suffering of winter, while traders and the wealthy maintain cheer and opportunity. The settlement is practical, suspicious, and strict about closing its gates at sundown. searchIndex.name: Gernerum
searchIndex.summary: A destroyed town remembered for its famous Icebeach figures and its fiery end after a mechanical dragon battle.
searchIndex.description: Gernerum is gone, leaving ruins, ash, and stories of a settlement that once shaped Icebeach before disaster consumed it.
searchIndex.searchText: Memory The guide remembers Gernerum as the childhood home or early refuge of figures tied to Icebeach history, including Thorn and Sylva Frostglade. Rumor Its only survivor is said to be the vile hag of the north, leaving the ruin with more dread than closure. searchIndex.name: Houlen Top
searchIndex.summary: The southern agricultural anomaly of Icebeach, where unwalled farmsteads produce grains and massive root vegetables.
searchIndex.description: Marked here as Houlen Top and described in the guide as Howlentop, this fertile valley feeds the north while keeping outsiders at the edge of town.
searchIndex.searchText: People The residents are physically imposing, guarded, and communal. They work with synchronized efficiency and rarely let strangers past the Border Market. Local oddities Full-moon curfews, refusal to handle silver, and the disappearance of predators or bandits make the town feel less undefended than it first appears. searchIndex.name: Icemoor
searchIndex.summary: An almost-abandoned watchtower settlement facing the Winrich Glacier and its fortress.
searchIndex.description: Icemoor is marked as a town on southern maps, but most cabins stand empty after families fled the glacier during the Eternal Winter.
searchIndex.searchText: The Watchers A skeleton crew of elderly holdouts maintains the tower and watches for movement from the glacier. They believe the silence is a trick and keep magical warning devices ready, though who receives those alerts is contested. Last stop For adventurers, Icemoor is the final warm meal before the white wastes. The Watchers record names in a ledger and expect most travelers never to return. Settlement IceBeach Watchtower Old Guard Winrich Glacier Abandoned Map IceBeach Status Mostly abandoned Watch Winrich Glacier and Winrich Fortress Residents The Old Guard, also called Custodians of the View

searchIndex.name: Little Rock Mentle Asylam
searchIndex.summary: A grim Gilded Nations asylum for criminals and dangerous minds deemed too risky for ordinary prisons.
searchIndex.description: Little Rock Mental Asylum is a remote containment institution where stone, sea, wards, and despair are all part of the security design.
searchIndex.searchText: Containment The asylum is described as the final destination for criminals, rogue mages, masterminds, killers, and political threats too dangerous to release or execute. Reputation Escape is treated as functionally impossible, and the place is said to leave no one unchanged even if they survive long enough to leave. searchIndex.name: Morana's Fang
searchIndex.summary: The tallest peak in the world, sacred to the Goddess of Winter and guarded by mysterious Icewind Sentinels.
searchIndex.description: Morana's Fang is a brutal pilgrimage mountain where the veil to divine and spirit realms thins near the Stillness Summit.
searchIndex.searchText: The climb The route crosses ice cliffs, wind-scoured ridges, deep crevasses, and the hunting grounds of cold-born monsters. The mountain tests endurance, resolve, and spirit rather than offering ordinary instruction. Sacred danger Legends say the summit once allowed direct communion with gods or spirits. Now it offers only cryptic visions, whispers on the wind, or encounters with servants of powers that still listen from the cold. searchIndex.name: Mt. Solaria
searchIndex.summary: A geothermal mountain of steam vents, salmon runs, failed mines, old tombs, and dragon rumors.
searchIndex.description: Mt. Solaria is a mountain of contradictions, with warmth venting through the cold and legends of an ancient wyrm beneath the gray sky.
searchIndex.searchText: Geothermal lure Steam vents and sudden thaws draw desperate settlers, fishers, and scholars despite avalanches, predators, and the fear that the dragon may stir. Old scars The slopes hold abandoned mines and ancient tomb facades, with rumors of cave-ins, territorial beasts, dragon cults, giant-kin remains, and draugr guarding mountain secrets. searchIndex.name: Ottiker
searchIndex.summary: A wine settlement on Sleetmond Lake, called Niror by locals and Ottiken by newer immigrants.
searchIndex.description: The town marked here as Ottiker is described in the guide as Niror or Ottiken, a frost-wine settlement caught between immigrant ambition and a bitter druidic feud.
searchIndex.searchText: Identity Astrousian and Last Elven State immigrants have reshaped the town, creating a visible clash between older local identity and new architecture, labor, and commerce. Wine conflict Niror Red has become valuable after the thaw, but shipments spike or fail when the feud with druids interferes. The injured Wyrm-Speaker governs through loyalists and a growing mercenary guard. Town IceBeach Niror Ottiken Wine Druids Dragonborn Map IceBeach Guide names Niror; Ottiken Industry Ice wine Leadership White Dragonborn Speaker Conflict Cold war with neighboring druids

searchIndex.name: Quilt
searchIndex.summary: A tiny Foaming Loch town of fish farming, dyed wool, and survival textiles warmed by nearby geothermal vents.
searchIndex.description: Quilt is a dockside maker-town whose fish farms and heavy Icesheep quilts depend on the Foaming Burrow keeping local waters alive.
searchIndex.searchText: The artisan economy Quilt exports heavy, colorful textiles woven from Icesheep wool. In the south, genuine Quilt tapestry has become a status symbol as much as survival gear. Geothermal dependence The town thrived through the Eternal Winter because nearby warm vents kept the waters usable, making the Burrow both a resource and something locals protect fiercely. Hamlet IceBeach Foaming Loch Aquaculture Icesheep Textiles Foaming Burrow Map IceBeach Size Smallest recognized Icebeach town Industries Aquaculture, dyed wool, quilts and tapestries Nearby The Foaming Burrow

searchIndex.name: Shiverwallow
searchIndex.summary: A fortified fishing town at the Chillfolk River, now operating its recovered fleet and winter ice camps.
searchIndex.description: Shiverwallow is a hard-working harbor of palisades, breakwaters, fish, smoke, and people shaped by years of frozen-sea survival.
searchIndex.searchText: Fleet reborn During the Eternal Winter the harbor froze solid, trapping ships and forcing camps onto the ice. Nine years later, the fleet is free again and the harbor is a forest of masts, nets, crews, and salted catch. Ice Walkers When winter sea ice returns, part of the population still migrates onto the floes to hunt seals and ice-whales, a tradition admired and feared even by other locals. searchIndex.name: Sleetmond
searchIndex.summary: A druidic lakeside settlement of sugar maples, fish, Icesheep, and the Hope Tree.
searchIndex.description: Sleetmond is a small town on Sleetmond Lake where druids and rangers tend the Hope Tree, sugar maple orchards, fish, and unusually warm Icesheep wool.
searchIndex.searchText: Druidic practice The town is notable for druidic traditions centered on the Hope Tree. Its people and practices are strange enough that many outsiders and even some natives distrust them. Survival economy Sugar maples, lake fish, and Icebeach sheep make Sleetmond more self-sufficient than many northern settlements. searchIndex.name: The Foaming Burrow
searchIndex.summary: A geothermal cave network southeast of Quilt that feeds the Foaming Loch and Foaming Runs.
searchIndex.description: The Foaming Burrow is not one cave but a network of steam vents, hot springs, and heated tunnels beneath a snow-free patch of ground.
searchIndex.searchText: Ecology Fire-resistant creatures, salamanders, magmin, druids, and elemental guardians are all plausible inhabitants of its hot chambers. Local tie Its heat keeps downstream waters from freezing and even supplies the Firenewt tea pets used by the Fireside Newt and Chai en' Steep Inn. searchIndex.name: The Hope Tree
searchIndex.summary: A warm, green-gold miracle tree that anchors Sleetmond and resists Morana's winter.
searchIndex.description: The Hope Tree rises impossibly in the frozen north, radiating warmth, safety, and restorative magic where Morana's cold should rule.
searchIndex.searchText: Sacred theories Most locals treat it as a blessing of Hestia, though other stories name Pythia, Bethtox, or an old divine confrontation with Morana as the reason the cold fails here. Restorative power Its leaves remain green and gold and can be brewed into healing teas, making the tree a symbol of community and a resource no sane local would willingly harm. searchIndex.name: Thrawbreak
searchIndex.summary: A remote mountain hamlet of ruined defenses, frozen docks, hard beer, and cut-off resentment.
searchIndex.description: Thrawbreak began as a mountaineer camp below the Auruan mountains and now survives between failed fortifications, a frozen harbor, and one known pass.
searchIndex.searchText: Isolation With the ferry from Whitedrift shut down, Thrawbreak is cut off by mountains, ice, and snow. Its people believe the rest of the world abandoned them. Local trouble Recent mysterious break-ins and the speaker's drunken night patrols add paranoia to a town already surviving on stubbornness and a tavern that never seems to run dry. searchIndex.name: Whitedrift
searchIndex.summary: A rocky Curse Run settlement watching the glacier, the fortress, and the asylum nearby.
searchIndex.description: Whitedrift clings to the mouth of the Curse Run, fed by Winrich Glacier melt, and carries the instability of people stationed too close to horror for too long.
searchIndex.searchText: Population Some residents are assigned to keep watch on the glacier and fortress, while others are said to be escapees or castoffs from the asylum. Atmosphere The settlement feels unstable by design: a cold rock town where glacial water, institutional shadow, and paranoia all meet. searchIndex.name: Winrich Fortress
searchIndex.summary: The black-stone ruin of Winrich, remembered as perhaps the first mortal lich.
searchIndex.description: Winrich Fortress drinks light from the glacier wind and remains a decaying monument to ancient necromancy, traps, undead, and deliberate misdirection.
searchIndex.searchText: Purpose Legends claim the fortress stood over a dark confluence called the soul well, but some scholars think Winrich built it as a decoy to hide his true phylactery and treasures elsewhere. Current danger The ruin is shunned for lesser undead, undetonated traps, psychic residue, and periodic spectral light similar to the glow reported inside Winrich Glacier. searchIndex.name: Wynwood Peak
searchIndex.summary: A smaller but treacherous peak covered in iron-hard woods and haunted by dragon-mound stories.
searchIndex.description: Wynwood Peak is less imposing in height than other mountains but feared for unnatural timber, difficult slopes, and the lingering evil of a ruined wizard tower.
searchIndex.searchText: Wynwood timber The trees are said to resist axe and saw, with roots that anchor into stone and wood that may carry protective magic from an ancient dragon burial. The tower A wizard drawn by the peak's rumored energies went mad and evil here. Though defeated, the tower remains feared for haunting and a hostile spirit bound to the mountain. searchIndex.name: Ded Moros Forest
searchIndex.summary: A grim woodland of petrified trees, old curse stories, and creatures adapted to stone-like forest remains.
searchIndex.description: Ded Moros Forest is not dead so much as unnaturally preserved, with gray stone trees, fossilized leaves, sharp branches, and roots that turn the forest floor into a maze.

searchIndex.name: Frostmaple Grove
searchIndex.summary: An ancient wild heartwood of unnaturally large frostmaples, sweet air, and slumbering treant guardians.
searchIndex.description: Frostmaple Grove is believed to be the primordial source of Sleetmond's sugar maple orchards, with gold-touched leaves and thick old bark even in deep winter.

searchIndex.name: Foaming Loch
searchIndex.summary: A geothermal lake whose warm, restless waters sustain Quilt and feed the Foaming Runs even through IceBeach's deepest cold.
searchIndex.description: The Foaming Loch lies in a basin of snow and dark stone, its surface broken by mist, mineral foam, and patches of open water warmed from below. Heat flowing from the Foaming Burrow keeps the lake alive through the northern winter, supporting Quilt's fish farms before the turbulent water continues into the Foaming Runs.

searchIndex.name: Sleetmond Lake
searchIndex.summary: A broad northern lake shared by Sleetmond and Ottiker, sustaining fishing, orchards, Icesheep, and the region's prized frost-wine.
searchIndex.description: Sleetmond Lake stretches beneath the northern sky between the druidic settlement of Sleetmond and the vineyards of Ottiker. Its cold waters provide fish for nearby communities, while sugar maples, grazing Icesheep, and the grapes used for Niror Red flourish along its shores. When the sky is clear, auroras ripple across the lake's broad surface.

searchIndex.name: Starcaller's Grove
searchIndex.summary: A bright-sky standing-stone grove where auroras, stars, and divination feel unusually near.
searchIndex.description: Starcaller's Grove stands apart from the snow drifts, with clearer skies, brighter stars, vibrant auroras, and moss-covered stones arranged in old patterns.

searchIndex.name: The Foaming Runs
searchIndex.summary: A turbulent river course of rapids, foam, steam, and geothermal vents fed from a cave source.
searchIndex.description: The Foaming Runs are marked by churning whitewater where icy river flow meets underground heat, producing dangerous steam and foam.

searchIndex.name: The Frigid Plains
searchIndex.summary: A vast wind-scoured tundra of whiteouts, monster hunts, hidden battlefields, and haunted snow.
searchIndex.description: The Frigid Plains are featureless and dangerous, with sudden whiteouts that punish poor navigation and expose travelers to the worst open tundra conditions.

searchIndex.name: Winrich Glacier
searchIndex.summary: A sickly green-blue glacier tied to Winrich, old necromancy, and horrors still preserved in the ice.
searchIndex.description: Winrich Glacier dominates Icebeach fear: a frozen mass associated with the first lich, dark ruins, and the sense that silence from the ice is never truly safe.

searchIndex.name: Gelwood
searchIndex.summary: A frontier town rebuilt on old stone and drawing settlers and prospectors.

searchIndex.name: Barthan's Traders
searchIndex.description: Run by Barthan Ironhand, a retired dwarven prospector with a kindly smile and hands like worn stone, this shop is the heart of Gelwood's commerce. The air within smells of sawdust, cured leather, and pickling spices. Barthan's stocks everything a settler could need, from sturdy axes and mining equipment to bolts of wool cloth, dried rations, and medicinal herbs. He is a font of local knowledge and is always willing to share a bit of news or a useful rumor with his customers.

searchIndex.name: Edermath Orchard
searchIndex.description: This beautiful orchard is tended by the Edermath family, a quiet half-elven clan who claim their ancestors planted the original trees centuries ago. The orchard miraculously survived the downfall of the previous settlement and was reclaimed from the wild by the family. They cultivate exceptionally crisp, tart apples and produce a famously potent cider that is a favorite at the Sleeping Giant tavern. The grove is known for its serene, almost unnaturally peaceful atmosphere.

searchIndex.name: Shrine To All
searchIndex.description: Rather than a single temple, this sacred space is an open-air collection of small, hand-built shrines nestled within the crumbling stone walls of an ancient ruin. Each alcove is dedicated to a different deity, reflecting the diverse faiths of the settlers who came seeking a new life. Offerings of wildflowers, carved wooden figures, and coins are left by the hopeful. The shrine is quietly maintained by an elderly woman named Lena, who ensures that all gods, great and small, are shown their due respect.

searchIndex.name: Sleeping Giant
searchIndex.description: Named for the massive, dormant mountain peak visible from its front door, this ale house is Gelwood's rowdiest establishment. Run by a boisterous and sharp-witted retired sellsword named Grelka, it is the favored haunt of prospectors, trappers, and traders. The air is thick with pipe smoke, the smell of spilled ale, and the sound of tall tales being spun. The 'Giant's Brew,' a dark and deceptively strong ale, is the tavern's signature drink and the cause of many morning regrets.

searchIndex.name: Smithy
searchIndex.description: The constant, rhythmic clang of a hammer on steel is the heartbeat of Gelwood, emanating from this open-air smithy built into the sturdy foundation of an old watchtower. The smith is a powerfully built and taciturn woman named Brynn. She specializes in crafting and repairing the tools of the trade: sharp axes, durable pickaxes, and reliable shovel heads. While she can mend a sword or forge a helmet, her true passion lies in creating practical, long-lasting tools for the hardworking folk of the town.

searchIndex.name: Stonehill Inn
searchIndex.description: As the only inn in Gelwood, Stonehill provides a much-needed respite for weary travelers and a quieter social hub for the locals. It is run by a warm and welcoming halfling couple, Erion and Miri Stonehill. The rooms are modest but always impeccably clean, and Miri's hearty rabbit stew is renowned along the Ronceval Road. The common room, with its crackling hearth, is a more family-friendly alternative to the Sleeping Giant, offering warm meals and softer conversation.

searchIndex.name: Barony of Fôret
searchIndex.description: A barony known for its exceptional hunters, fishers, and miners, who are fierce independence.

searchIndex.name: Barony of Pierrefond
searchIndex.description: A pragmatic industrial barony, the House du Rocher's quiet power comes from its control over the kingdom's vital manufacturing, production, and mining.

searchIndex.name: The Barony of Aquitaine
searchIndex.description: The Barony of Aquitaine is a wealthy and opportunistic barony that gains its power from commerce, trade guilds, its powerful merchant fleet, the capital being within its lands, and its loyalty to Queen Eloise I.

searchIndex.name: The Barony of Lac
searchIndex.description: The Barony of Lac is an enigmatic and reclusive region ruled by the mystical House du Lac, who are deeply connected to the land's ancient secrets.

searchIndex.name: The Barony of Lorraine
searchIndex.description: A proud region, the House de Lorraine is called the homeland of Kings as acient kings were born here and the current Queen hid here during he hiding.

searchIndex.name: The Barony of Montaigne
searchIndex.description: A fiercely militaristic mountain people, the House de Montfort values strength and discipline above all else. They see themselves as the line between Arfordir and other.

searchIndex.name: The Port City of Stomion
searchIndex.summary: A hard-edged river-delta port of docks, districts, and imperial pressure.

searchIndex.name: Baths of the Devine Mother
searchIndex.summary: A pristine, marble-clad sanctuary and bathhouse dedicated to Pythia, featuring lush gardens and a natural warm spring that serves as a quiet, neutral retreat for the city's elite.
searchIndex.description: An oasis of pristine white marble and verdant greenery amidst the smog of Stomion, the Baths of the Divine Mother are a sanctuary dedicated to Pythia, the Primordial Lifegiver.
searchIndex.searchText: Context Fed by the city's only remaining natural spring, the water is naturally warm and famed for its revitalizing properties. The interior is a humidity-filled paradise where exotic flora—blessed by the influence of Veridia—thrives under skylights and soft candlelight, defying the harsh industrial climate outside. A breathtaking statue of Pythia stands at the center of the main pool, her arms outstretched as if offering the waters to the bathers below. Operated by the Lifewardens and a quiet staff of attendants, the facility maintains a strict policy of equality; within these walls, nobles and merchants bathe side-by-side without segregation, weapons, or rank, though the clientele remains largely exclusive due to its location. Silence is heavily encouraged, allowing the sound of trickling water to dominate the air. High Warden Thyleesha currently manages the baths, though she grows increasingly anxious as recent industrial run-off from the neighboring districts threatens to taint the ancient, mysterious source of their holy spring. The Port City of Stomion Map The Port City of Stomion

searchIndex.name: Beccin Chancery Embasy
searchIndex.summary: The imposing stone headquarters of the Vardenheim Directorate, ruled by the clinical and ruthless Overseer Verrick, serving as the true center of Imperial control and secret police operations.
searchIndex.description: Constructed within what was once a public park, the Beccin Embassy is a monolithic palace of cold, solid stone that feels utterly alien amidst the weathered architecture of Oldfort.
searchIndex.searchText: Context It serves as the headquarters for the Vardenheim Directorate and the seat of Overseer Intendant Verrick, the 'Hand of the Emperor.' Verrick is a 'Sanitized Tyrant' who views the occupation not as a war, but as a failing factory requiring correction; he wears pristine white gloves to metaphorically and literally keep the filth of the city at bay. The interior is chillingly cold and decorated with imposing propaganda of the Emperor. While the upper floors are a maze of dismissively polite bureaucracy where meetings are nearly impossible to secure, the lower levels house the Directorate's interrogation cells. It is guarded by a specialized detachment of the City Watch, ensuring that Verrick's industrial dismantling of the rebellion proceeds without interruption. The Port City of Stomion Diplomacy Map The Port City of Stomion

searchIndex.name: Breads and Dregs
searchIndex.summary: A popular bakery-tavern in Northgate offering lodging, strong coffee, and famous 'Road Kits' for travelers, known for its warm atmosphere and century-old sourdough starter.
searchIndex.description: A chaotic, warm, and wonderfully loud establishment that serves as the beating heart of Northgate's social scene.
searchIndex.searchText: Context Breads and Dregs acts as both a premier bakery and a tavern, catering to weary travelers and locals alike. The air is permanently thick with the comforting scent of yeast and roasting grains, obscuring the smell of the city outside. They are famous for their 'Road Kits'—pre-wrapped ration packs of hardtack, dried meats, and cheese—and a legendary sourdough starter rumored to be over a century old and perhaps slightly sentient. The tavern offers lodging upstairs, and the common room is a dog-friendly haven where local bands play at night and sleepy wagon-drivers fuel up on strong coffee at dawn. It is a place of transit, where the 'dregs' refers affectionately to the bottom of a good cup of coffee or ale, shared among friends. searchIndex.name: Cat and Hound
searchIndex.summary: A cozy, evening-only tavern run by two sisters, offering cheap, hearty food and a welcoming atmosphere on a lowered building near the train tracks.
searchIndex.description: The Cat and Hound is a warm, cozy sanctuary situated on a raised mezzanine level overlooking the street, its timbers vibrating gently with the rhythmic passing of nearby trains.
searchIndex.searchText: Context Owned by the sisters Kallista and Eleni, the tavern is a beloved staple for the city's mid-level workers looking for a quiet evening. Kallista, a stoic veteran of the national army, is known as 'The Hound,' while the tavern's name serves as a quiet, melancholic memorial to her lost lover, a Felis—'The Cat'—who vanished during the war. While Kallista handles security and the heavy lifting, Eleni, who worked the floor under the previous owner, manages the patrons with practiced grace. They are famous for serving high-quality meals at unbeatable prices, a feat accomplished by the sisters personally scouring the markets at dawn to source fresh ingredients themselves. Open only from 4 PM to midnight, the tavern enforces strict rules against politics and magic, allowing patrons to enjoy the piano music and hearty stew while the owners secretly harbor sympathies for the rebellion. searchIndex.name: Govenors Gate
searchIndex.summary: An ancient, fortified Elven gatehouse guarding the bridge to Aelindor's Isle, manned by corrupt City Watch and nicknamed 'The Traitor's Arch'.
searchIndex.description: Locally reviled as 'The Traitor's Arch,' the Governor's Gate is a structure of ancient, gorgeous Elven stonework that serves as the choke point between the city and the puppet administration on Aelindor's Isle.
searchIndex.searchText: Context The gatehouse consists of two square, crenellated towers flanking a heavy, reinforced arched entry at the end of a long stone causeway. It is not manned by the elite Beccin Black Guard, but by a hand-picked detachment of the City Watch. These guards enforce a strict 'official business only' policy, processing visitors with invasive searches and mandatory escorts—unless, of course, one can pay the steep bribes they are known to accept. In the past, the gate was a gathering point for desperate refugees begging for aid, but the terrifying silhouette of the Beccin airship hovering just above the castle has largely scared them away, leaving the bridge eerily quiet. searchIndex.name: Governor's Castle
searchIndex.summary: The ancient Elven Castle Aelindor, now the seat of the puppet Magistrate Vael, a collaborator trapped between a hateful populace and the ruthless Beccin Empire.
searchIndex.description: Commonly known as the Governor's Castle, this structure is historically Castle Aelindor, an ancient Elven fortress of elegant and sea-facing balconies.
searchIndex.searchText: Context It is currently the seat of Magistrate Vael, the nervous and sweating face of the 'Traitor Elf' administration. Clad in an ill-fitting Beccin tunic that symbolizes her uncomfortable submission, Vael stands paralyzed between a populace that loathes her collaboration and an Empire that views her softness as an inefficiency. She rules in name only, reading decrees of quarantine and tax hikes to angry crowds from the safety of the castle walls, while the black shadow of a Beccin airship hovers perpetually overhead. Unknown to her, she is merely a puppet being groomed by Overseer Verrick. The Port City of Stomion Seat of power Map The Port City of Stomion

searchIndex.name: Hags Hovel
searchIndex.summary: A seedy tavern in The Shacks built from an expanded tugboat, run by a cantankerous old woman and guarded by a massive Dragonborn, serving as a safe haven for illicit deals.
searchIndex.description: Within the chaotic sprawl of The Shacks lies Hags Hovel, a notorious dive bar built from the rusted hull of a scavenged tugboat that has been aggressively expanded with bolted-on scrap and driftwood.
searchIndex.searchText: Context The establishment earns its name from its proprietor, an unpleasant and razor-tongued old woman whose eclectic collection of personal trinkets lines the grime-slicked walls. The roof is a sieve of leaks caught by a maze of buckets, and the air is thick with the smell of wet rot and desperation. Imperial patrols avoid the venue entirely, making it a sanctuary for the city's criminal element; while the house doesn't sell contraband, the patrons openly do. A back room hosts high-stakes gambling and hushed contracts, all enforced by 'Kiddo,' a massive Dragonborn bouncer who ensures that the lawlessness remains organized. searchIndex.summary: A magic school formerly known as Xylokoilo, where students are strictly trained for military service and failure results in severe cognitive decline.
searchIndex.description: Formerly known as the Xylokoilo Lyceum (Ancient for 'Woodhollow'), this institution was rebranded to align with the modern sensibilities of the Beccin occupation.
searchIndex.searchText: Context It is named after Hera Vlachouli, a figure sympathetic to the Empire, helping to ease the local populace's disdain for the wizarding class that largely fled the country. Led by Headmistress Elpida Tata, who walks a razor-thin line between Imperial loyalty and academic preservation, the Institute focuses on producing magically capable assets for the Beccin military. The curriculum is rigorous, strictly categorized, and heavily monitored; Wild Magic is treated as a dangerous pathology to be suppressed. Students wear robes blending classical Greek drapes with color-coded house linings. Failure is not an option—those who wash out are sent to 'remedial programs' from which they return noticeably simpler and mentally eroded. Beneath the school lies a sealed subterranean complex now known as 'The Deeproot,' rumored to hold secrets from the school's older, wilder days. searchIndex.summary: Merchant's Hill is an elite residential district for the city's 'Old Money,' characterized by owner-maintained ornate street lamps, polite social exclusion, and the Public Observatory.
searchIndex.description: Rising above the smog of the lower city, Merchant's Hill is the residential enclave of Stomion's 'Old Money.'
searchIndex.searchText: Context It is a neighborhood of fading but dignified elegance, home to wealthy regional merchants and ancient families who cling to the pre-occupation past. While the residents possess little actual political authority—having been stripped of real power by the Beccin administration—they maintain a stubborn veneer of influence through social exclusion and a culture that is 'snobby, but not overly rude.' The district is visually defined by its unique lighting: rather than uniform municipal posts, the streets are illuminated by ornate, distinct oil lamps. Each lamp is commissioned and zealously maintained by the owner of the nearest manor as a fierce display of status and wealth. The area is not gated but is heavily patrolled by the City Watch, who politely ensure that the uninvited do not linger. Notable residents include Veylan Wollif, the envoy for the Iron Coffer. The district’s crown jewel is the Public Observatory, a place of quiet contemplation where the elite watch the stars, ignoring the industrial smoke rising from the districts below. searchIndex.searchText: Context It serves as the private botanical conservatory and primary social salon for those in the Synedrion of Blood. Inside, the air is perfumed and perfectly humidified, maintained by complex weather wards that nurture flora extinct everywhere else in Eschatia. Silver-ferns from the Lost Age and glowing moon-blooming lotuses. searchIndex.description: Welcome to The Shop!
searchIndex.searchText: Context Back in the glory days, this facility was a premier, open-floor smithy. Now? It’s a survival rig adapted for the grind. We stripped the layout and partitioned it into flats to house a crew of makers and their families. The main floor got squeezed, but it remains the beating heart of the operation: a high-traffic, communal fabrication zone where every discipline from leather-working to cold forging collides. We keep a resident fabricator on site, bunked in a solo unit. They machine the components, true the grinding wheels, and repair the communal gear. In exchange for keeping the shop running, the rest of the crew knows when to look the other way. If a shipment of non-standard, unregistered materials hits the loading dock? We didn't see a thing. searchIndex.name: Academy Gardens
searchIndex.summary: A wealthy park district surrounding Hera Vlachouli’s Institute, where manicured gardens, public spellwork, and magical lights create one of Stomion’s most elegant public spaces.
searchIndex.description: Academy Gardens surrounds Hera Vlachouli’s Institute of the Arcane with winding waterways, immaculate lawns, and shaded walking paths. Students practice magic beneath the trees while wealthy residents stroll grounds maintained by unseen servants. Though open to the public, nightly patrols preserve the district’s carefully ordered atmosphere.

searchIndex.name: Aelindor's Isle
searchIndex.summary: A restricted government island centered on ancient Castle Aelindor, guarded by a fortified bridge and overshadowed by the Beccin occupation.
searchIndex.description: Aelindor’s Isle rises from the water in salt-darkened cliffs, weathered rock shelves, and narrow ledges softened by manicured gardens. Ancient Castle Aelindor serves as the seat of state administration, reached through a single heavily guarded bridge, while a black Beccin airship hangs above its Elven spires.

searchIndex.name: Brighttfyr
searchIndex.summary: A holy district at the river mouth where priests keep the High Beacon burning through every watch to guide ships into Stomion.
searchIndex.description: Brighttfyr occupies Stomion’s rocky downriver point, its salt-streaked stone and bright glass washed by the High Beacon’s immense oil flame. Clerics of Origin and Bethtox divide each day into four watches to keep the light burning, guiding ships through the river mouth while the district hums long after the rest of the city sleeps.

searchIndex.name: Cathedral
searchIndex.summary: The highest point on Stomion’s main island, crowned by a grand public sanctuary honoring gods from across the pantheons.
searchIndex.description: The Cathedral crowns the highest point on Stomion’s main island, its beautiful sanctuary open to worshippers of many faiths. Priests of the most widely revered gods tend prominent shrines within the main hall, while smaller statues, alcoves, and offerings honor the countless other deities of the pantheons. It is a shared place of prayer rather than the seat of any single faith.

searchIndex.name: Coin's Curve
searchIndex.summary: Stomion’s heavily guarded financial district, where banks and counting houses overlook an open railway and rumored vaults reach deep beneath the streets.
searchIndex.description: Coin’s Curve sits above the sweeping bend of an open rail cut, with stone banks, counting houses, and financial temples lining the streets along its rim. The clatter of trains rises from below—the sound of money, as bankers call it—while private guards in polished plate enforce dress codes and bar anyone without business. After closing, the district empties into silence above vaults rumored to be carved deep into the bedrock.

searchIndex.name: Harrowholm
searchIndex.summary: Harrowholm is the fortified island seat of the City Mayor and City Watch, named for an ancient noble sacrifice that haunts the site.
searchIndex.description: Connected to the city by a long, defensible stone bridge, Harrowholm is a small, fortified island that serves as the seat of Stomion’s municipal government. The district is named for 'The Harrowing,' a tragic historical event where the city's ancient noble family sacrificed themselves to seal a gate to the Shadowfell—an act that infused their surviving bloodline with latent sorcerous power. The island is dominated by a distinctive round tower which houses the headquarters of the City Watch on its lower levels, while the upper levels serve as the residence for the current Mayor, Thaddeus Vane, and his family. Mayor Vane is widely regarded as a weak leader who works far too comfortably with the Beccin occupiers, creating a local government that operates autonomously in name only. He rules with a small circle of appointed officials, protected from the tax-paying populace that elected him by the surrounding waters and the City Watch barracks beneath his floorboards. Rumors persist among the guards that the island is haunted by the shadows of the original noble sacrifice, and deep beneath the tower lies a dungeon that holds more than just common criminals.

searchIndex.name: Highhammer
searchIndex.summary: Highhammer is a pristine, Dwarf-majority district housing the Temple of Matrix and the showrooms of the Ossurian Forges.
searchIndex.description: A district of imposing stone and polished brass, Highhammer stands as a meticulously curated monument to Dwarven industry and destiny. This area is kept unnervingly clean—a 'model district' designed to showcase the might of the Ossurian Forges to the occupied populace. The skyline is dominated by The High Hammer of Matrix, a temple dedicated to the God of the Forge and Destiny who liberated the dwarves from their ancient oppressor. The temple is marked by a colossal, ornamental hammer suspended above its entrance, a symbol of the destiny forged within. The streets are lined with the high-end showrooms of the Beccin Empire's military industrial complex, displaying gleaning weapons and marvels. While these storefronts are open to the public, the workshops behind them are restricted zones. The district is primarily inhabited by Dwarves—both Ossurian expats and local artisans. It is also the location of the 'Old Furnace.'

searchIndex.name: Merchant's Hill
searchIndex.summary: An old-money residential district of private manors, ornate street lamps, and polite but persistent exclusion.
searchIndex.description: Merchant’s Hill is Stomion’s old-money residential enclave, preserving the fading elegance of families wealthy before the occupation. Each household commissions the ornate oil lamp nearest its property, turning the streets into a quiet competition of glass, metalwork, and family taste. The district is not formally gated, but City Watch patrols politely ensure that uninvited visitors do not linger.

searchIndex.name: Mirkwater
searchIndex.summary: A crowded working waterfront of workshops, cramped housing, and small trade, where Stomion’s makers and off-ledger economy stay in motion.
searchIndex.description: Mirkwater is a dense, practical waterfront where workshops, subdivided flats, handcarts, and small traders compete for every dry patch of street. Places such as the Shop combine housing and fabrication beneath the same roof, with workers sharing heat, tools, and loading space. The district is loud, crowded, and full of people accustomed to repairing what the city cannot afford to replace.

searchIndex.name: Mirkwwater Landing
searchIndex.summary: A working landing serving Mirkwater, where passengers, materials, and cargo move between the neighborhood and the water.
searchIndex.description: Mirkwwater Landing is Mirkwater’s direct connection to the water, handling the district’s everyday flow of passengers, supplies, and small cargo. Practical and busy rather than formal, it links the landing traffic with Mirkwater’s workshops, traders, and crowded streets.

searchIndex.name: Newkort
searchIndex.summary: A dense residential district of tenements, narrow family homes, bakeries, and food stalls, favored by mid-ranking Beccin and State officials.
searchIndex.description: Newkort is a dense residential district of crowded tenements and narrow single-family dwellings built shoulder to shoulder. Many mid-ranking Beccin and State officials and officers make their homes here, giving the neighborhood a respectable character without the wealth of Stomion’s grander districts. Bakeries and food stalls occupy ground floors and street corners, serving residents from early morning into the evening.

searchIndex.name: Northgate
searchIndex.summary: Northgate is a busy, family-friendly district defined by overland trade and traveler amenities, funeral parlor, and conselor center.
searchIndex.description: Renamed for its location adjacent to the city's North Gate, this district is a bustling hub of overland travelers. The streets are perpetually active with wagons hauling lumber and fresh produce from the northern fields. It is a welcoming, family-safe neighborhood characterized by practical homes, local bakeries, and taverns that specialize in hearty stews and warm beds for weary road-weary visitors. While a small contingent of Beccin Imperial guards maintains a visible presence at the gate itself, the district's true anchor is the House of the Lost and Wayward. It is a respectable funeral parlor and counseling center staffed by doctor-like professionals and funded by open donations.

searchIndex.name: Oldfort
searchIndex.summary: The historic heart of Stomion, where the ancient city administration building is physically and metaphorically overshadowed by the massive, modern Beccin Embassy, creating a district of bureaucracy.
searchIndex.description: As the oldest district in Stomion, Oldfort is a jarring collision of eras. The district centers on the titular 'Old Fort,' a weathered stone structure that once defended the coast but now serves as the weary heart of municipal administration. However, it is the Beccin Embassy that truly dominates the skyline; a massive, modern structure of red brick and glass that has been annexed onto the ancient fort, nearly eclipsing it in size and standing as a physical manifestation of the occupation. During the day, the streets are a chaotic sea of misery and opportunism: long, snaking lines of citizens wait hours to pay the 'Math Tax' or plead for permits, while 'fixers,' scribes, and disbarred lawyers buzz through the crowds selling shortcuts. The air is thick with the smell of ink, despair, and ozone. Yet, the moment the clock strikes 4:30 PM, the district dies instantly. The shutters slam down, the bureaucrats flee, and Oldfort becomes a ghost town of silent stone and ticking clocks.

searchIndex.name: Oldmarket
searchIndex.summary: Stomion’s historic wholesale market and civic-commercial center, home to the Merchant Senate and Imperial Offices.
searchIndex.description: Oldmarket is one of Stomion’s historic trading districts, where goods pass through warehouses before being divided among the city’s smaller markets and shops. The Merchant Senate and Imperial Offices stand among its warehouses and public buildings, placing local commerce and State administration side by side. An old public bath survives among the district’s busier institutions.

searchIndex.name: Roselantern
searchIndex.summary: Stomion’s late-night district of music, performance, food, companionship, and arcades both old and new.
searchIndex.description: Roselantern is Stomion’s district of nightlife, art, and celebration. Musicians, performers, professional companions, tavernkeepers, and food sellers keep its streets lively after dark. Traditional covered arcades shelter shops, cafés, and small stages, while newer amusement halls offer mechanical games, magical diversions, and contests of skill. Warm colored lanterns illuminate the revelry long after the city’s working districts have closed.

searchIndex.name: Saltmarket
searchIndex.summary: An open waterfront market stretching between Stomion’s two docks, where daily trade shares space with public announcements and gatherings.
searchIndex.description: Saltmarket stretches between Stomion’s two docks as a broad open-air marketplace and public gathering ground. Vendors sell salt, fish, preserved food, and harbor provisions around a central space kept open for civic notices, proclamations, speeches, and other announcements. On busy days, dockworkers, sailors, merchants, and residents turn the district into one of the city’s loudest meeting places.

searchIndex.name: Side Harbor
searchIndex.summary: Stomion’s international working harbor, where foreign crews, trading houses, naval officials, and local dock labor meet.
searchIndex.description: Side Harbor is Stomion’s international working harbor, where foreign flags and unfamiliar languages mingle with dock bells, cargo crews, and local traffic. The Imperial Admiralty watches from offices along the waterfront, while foreign concerns such as the Wolgari Trading Company maintain their own docks and houses of trade. Sailors, commercial agents, harbor officials, and laborers keep the quays busy through every arrival and departure.

searchIndex.name: Smartwalk
searchIndex.summary: A civic and professional district of State offices, magic shops, hired carriages, and busy communications.
searchIndex.description: Smartwalk is Stomion’s working civic district, centered on the State Government Building and local administration; no Beccin offices operate here. State clerks, advocates, couriers, and visitors share its streets with magic shops and specialist businesses. Taxis and open buggies wait for fares while communications lines carry a steady stream of official and commercial traffic through the district.

searchIndex.name: Steamwall
searchIndex.summary: A uninhabited industrial utility district defined by a dense tangle of hissing pipes and chemical vents.
searchIndex.description: The Steamwall is a dedicated industrial zone defined not by walls of stone, but by a dense, hissing curtain of vents and pressurized piping. The air here is thick with smog and strange, unnaturally colored chemical vapors that swirl under the light of sickly yellow oil lamps, which burn day and night to cut through the haze. It serves as the component heart of the city's production, churning out gears, rivets, and refined fuel to feed the factories elsewhere. Unlike the state-run facilities, the Steamwall is privately held—the Beccin Empire explicitly owns nothing here, leaving the district in the hands of ruthlessly efficient private consortiums. It is a district of pure utility; the smell of copper and metal hangs heavy, and while the noise of grinding machinery is deafening by day, the area empties completely at night, as no one is willing to live amidst the toxic fumes.

searchIndex.name: The Badges
searchIndex.summary: A surprisingly accessible residential district housing Beccin soldiers, local 'Grey' forces, and their families, defined by high morale, imperial propaganda, and exclusive amenities superior to the rest of the city.
searchIndex.description: 'The Badges' is the dedicated residential enclave for the city's martial forces, housing both the occupying Beccin troops and the local 'Grey' collaborators. Contrary to the expected segregation, the housing here is of uniformly decent quality for both factions, fostering a sense of unified purpose rather than hierarchy. It is a district of families as much as soldiers, filled with the bustling domestic life of those on the empire's payroll. The streets are washed in the colors of the Empire, draped heavily in flags and patriotic propaganda to keep morale high. The district's most envied features are its exclusive commissaries—well-stocked stores that offer goods and luxuries often unavailable or unaffordable to the general public. Despite its military nature, the district is not a closed fortress; it remains surprisingly open to the city at large, projecting an image of confidence and integration rather than fear.

searchIndex.name: The Bulwark
searchIndex.summary: A fortified sequence of bridges, causeways, gates, and guard stations spanning the vast natural chasm that separates Aelindor’s Isle from Stomion.
searchIndex.description: The Bulwark is not a single wall, but a layered defensive crossing built across the vast natural chasm separating Aelindor’s Isle from the rest of Stomion. Merchant Gate anchors the cityward approach, while narrow bridges, stone causeways, and reinforced guard stations lead toward Governor’s Gate and the final crossing to the island. Traffic can be stopped at several points long before anyone reaches the governor’s seat.

searchIndex.name: The Chimes
searchIndex.summary: The legacy-named hub of the high-end artisan district, characterized by soft music from ancient chimes, snobbish exclusivity, and the popular Azure Teapot tea house.
searchIndex.description: Chimgate is the cultural and commercial zenith of Stomion’s artisan district. Despite the name, no defensive gate stands here; the title is a legacy of the ancient wind chimes that once hung from every eave and archway 'back in the day.' A handful of these original chimes remain, filling the plaza with a soft, melodic background music that encourages hushed tones and polite behavior. This is a district of high-end commerce where the streets are uncrowded and the atmosphere is undeniably snobbish; one does not simply 'shop' at Chimgate, one selects fine jewelry, clothes, and art from masters of the craft. The clientele is a mix of wealthy tourists, established merchants, and high-ranking Beccin occupiers seeking to acquire local luxury. Deals are frequently finalized over delicate infusions at The Azure Teapot, the district's premier tea house.

searchIndex.name: The Hallow Heart
searchIndex.summary: Stomion’s central rail junction and water-tower district, named for the famed local inventor Valen Hallow.
searchIndex.description: The Hallow Heart is where the rail lines entering and leaving Stomion converge with the line to the Raildock. Water towers and three great bridges dominate the district, with only a handful of residences standing among the infrastructure. Named for the celebrated inventor Valen Hallow, the junction is vital to both the city’s transportation network and its water supply.

searchIndex.name: The Shacks
searchIndex.summary: A lawless, sprawling shantytown built from scavenged scrap on the city's fringe, inhabited by the desperate and those living 'off-ledger' largely ignored by Imperial patrols.
searchIndex.description: Description 'The Shacks' is a chaotic, unplanned warren of survival that clings to the edge of the city. True to its name, the district is composed almost entirely of improvised structures built from scavenged scrap metal, driftwood, and stolen industrial refuse. It is the refuge of the city’s poorest citizens, the displaced, and those who operate 'off-ledger' to survive the occupation. In a stark departure from the suffocating surveillance of the city center, Imperial patrols are shockingly rare here, effectively ceding the territory to locals and making it a dangerous but necessary haven for those needing to disappear.

searchIndex.name: The Swath
searchIndex.summary: A hard-scrabble rail-side district of crowded housing, labor yards, inexpensive taverns, and Stomion’s poorest residents.
searchIndex.description: The Swath is Stomion at its most hard-scrabble: dense, worn down, and constantly shaken by nearby rail traffic. Workers, families, and the city’s poorest residents crowd into buildings repeatedly divided, repaired, and repurposed, while taverns and food sellers offer affordable comfort between shifts. Freight, soot, and vibration from the Raildock shape the district’s daily rhythm.

searchIndex.name: The Towers
searchIndex.summary: An elite, restricted district of soaring spires and sky-bridges inhabited by sorcerers, lit by magical arc lamps and rumored to sit atop ancient crypts.
searchIndex.description: Rising high above the smog of Stomion, 'The Towers' serves as the exclusive, vertical enclave of the city's sorcerous elite. It is a district of soaring stone spires connected by elegant sky-bridges, allowing residents to traverse the area without ever touching the ground level. The atmosphere is distinct from the rest of the city; bathed in the cold, steady glow of blue-white magical arc lamps, it stands in sharp contrast to the flickering yellow gaslights of the Beccin occupation. Access is strictly controlled through a combination of physical checkpoints and magical ward-alarms that alert private security to unauthorized entrants; those caught without proper paperwork are stripped of their possessions and ejected. Inside, the Beccin presence is almost non-existent, leaving the powerful Great Houses to plot, dine in high-end bakeries, and flaunt the latest fashions in relative sovereignty. While the spires represent the height of luxury, the foundations are rumored to be honeycombed with ancient crypts holding the secrets—and remains—of a first sorcerers.

searchIndex.name: Wallside
searchIndex.summary: A small lower-middle-class residential district of modest, closely packed homes along Stomion’s outer wall.
searchIndex.description: Wallside is a small residential district built along Stomion’s outer wall. Its closely packed homes belong largely to working households with steady but limited incomes. Neither prosperous nor destitute, the neighborhood is defined by practical housing, careful maintenance, and families making the most of what they have.

searchIndex.name: Apsley
searchIndex.summary: Apsley is the cliffside capital of the Commonwealth of Half Height, famed for its trade, wealth, and white-stone terraces.
searchIndex.description: Apsley is the principal city and political heart of the Commonwealth of Half Height, rising in bright tiers of stone, stucco, and retaining walls from its busy docks to its sunlit upper terraces. Long admired as a free-port miracle, the city is known for its ministries, merchant houses, embassies, legal arcades, and the great gondola-funicular spine that binds its heights together. Yet Apsley’s prosperity rests upon a deep social divide: the upper wards enjoy ceremony, comfort, and influence, while the lower districts bear the burdens of freight, customs, industry, and unrest. Its culture is shaped by halfling household politics, public hospitality, and reputation-driven commerce, giving the city a reputation for both generosity and quiet coercion. To admirers, Apsley is proof that disciplined law and trade can secure independence in a dangerous world; to critics, it is a city of polished facades sustained by patronage, inequality, and carefully managed disorder.
searchIndex.searchText: At a glance Apsley rises in bright terraces from its harbor, with civic offices, embassies, and merchant houses stacked above the docks.
